assertion.statement: For each actual characteristic-zero Heegner field or local completion F, the finite Kummer sequence 0->E(F)/2^a E(F)->H1(F,E[2^a])->H1(F,E)[2^a]->0 is exact and its point map is additive, restriction-compatible and equivariant under field automorphisms.
assertion.objects: The fixed elliptic curve, actual M_I and H_f number fields, finite extensions of Q_p at old places, and their finite extensions.
assertion.hypotheses: F has characteristic0, E/F is an elliptic curve and a>=1; continuous Galois cohomology with discrete algebraic-point modules.
assertion.quantifiers: Every permitted field and positive finite coefficient stage; every point and cohomology class in the displayed groups.
assertion.parameter_range: n=2^a; all residue characteristics including2 for the local fields.
assertion.uniformity: The same construction is natural for the actual restrictions and field transports; no quantitative constant.
assertion.constants: No multiplier beyond the separately supplied local c_E enters the exact sequence.
assertion.normalizations: delta(P)(g)=gQ-Q for nQ=P; ordinary untwisted E[n] at the descent stage.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Does not supply CM points, norm relations, relative Galois groups, unramifiedness or local cohomology annihilation. No rational-torsion, good-reduction, rank or finite-Sha assumption.
assertion.limit_order: Establish surjectivity over the separable closure, construct the cocycle and prove exactness, then apply to point multiples or the separately annihilated restriction kernel.

use.reason: The actual number-field and local-field steps require the generic finite Kummer sequence, not the earlier Q-only forward Selmer specialization.
use.shared_contract_justification: All occurrences use the same characteristic-zero finite Kummer construction; the number-field step uses equivariance and vanishing on multiples, and the local step uses exactness after a separately supplied annihilator.

supplier.statement: For an elliptic curve over a field, multiplication by a nonzero integer is a nonconstant isogeny defined over the field; every nonzero isogeny is finite and surjective.

publication.title: The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves
publication.locator: SectionIII.4 opening p66; Example4.1 p67; Proposition4.2(a) p68.
publication.corrections: Original pages66–68 directly rendered and read. No uninspected erratum is used; this source claim is separate from known division-polynomial and two-isogeny display corrections elsewhere.

available_assertion.statement: For an elliptic curve over a field, multiplication by a nonzero integer is a nonconstant isogeny defined over the field; every nonzero isogeny is finite and surjective.
available_assertion.objects: Elliptic curves and their multiplication maps.
available_assertion.hypotheses: Elliptic curve over the source field; nonzero integer multiplication.
available_assertion.quantifiers: Every such elliptic curve and nonzero integer.
available_assertion.parameter_range: Used here only in characteristic0 with positive powers of2.
available_assertion.uniformity: Exact algebraic assertion independent of the arithmetic field or conductor.
available_assertion.constants: No numerical degree formula is required.
available_assertion.normalizations: Usual group-law multiplication, identity mapped to identity.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: Zero multiplication is excluded; this assertion does not itself state the Kummer cohomology sequence.
available_assertion.limit_order: Construct multiplication as a field-defined morphism, establish nonconstancy, then use surjectivity of a nonzero isogeny.
